paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, recorded as one paragraph entry per the pass instructions. The en field is identical to the zh field: every cell is a chemical symbol or a compound number, and the only German-language token on the page is the column head 'Nr.' (Nummer, i.e. No.), left as printed so the header row matches the source. The table continues from the preceding page and continues onto the next: it opens mid-sequence at Nr. 260 and breaks off after Nr. 286, and no Tabelle caption and no scaffold drawing appear on this page, so the shared substituents that caption fixes are not visible here and are not reproduced. Column heads are printed with superscripts, R with a raised 7a, 7b, 12 and 1; they are transcribed inline as R7a, R7b, R12, R1. The subscript digits in SO2, CH2CH2, OCH2CF3 and PhC(O)CH2 are printed as true subscripts and are likewise transcribed inline. Nr. 270 carries L = CH2CH2 while Nr. 271 and 272 in the same Bz block carry L = CHMe; that is what is printed and it is transcribed as printed, not regularised to the H/H, H/Me, Me/Me triple pattern the rest of the table follows. Nr. 270 is also the row where R1 switches from OCH2CF3 to O-c-Hexyl. The R12 cell of Nr. 265 is set one space further right than the PhSO2 entries above and below it; that is print alignment, not a different value, and the leading space is not carried into the transcription. A small stray ink mark sits over the O of OCH2CF3 in the R1 cell of Nr. 261, a faint dot sits in the Nr. cell of row 261 and another in the R7a cell of Nr. 280; all read as scan artifacts, not characters. The table body ends after Nr. 286 and the lower quarter of the page is blank.
